BYLAWS OF THE SOCIETY
(As amended up to the Special General Body Meeting held on 12 January 2024)

---

CHAPTER I – NAME, ADDRESS AND AREA OF OPERATION

1.1 Name of the Society:
The name of the Society shall be "Shanti Vihar Cooperative Housing Society Limited", hereinafter referred to as "the Society". The word "Limited" shall form part of the name of the Society in accordance with section 9(1) of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960.

1.2 Registered Address:
The registered office of the Society shall be at Flat No. A-102, Shanti Vihar, Plot No. 21, Sector 17, Vashi, Navi Mumbai – 400703, or at such other place within the local limits of the Thane District as may be decided by the General Body and approved by the Registrar.

1.3 Area of Operation:
The area of operation of the Society shall be confined to the property known as Shanti Vihar, situate at Plot No. 21, Sector 17, Vashi, Navi Mumbai, together with all structures, common areas, and appurtenances belonging to the Society.

1.4 Liability of Members:
The liability of the members of the Society shall be limited to the amount of share capital subscribed by each member, as provided under section 64 of the Act.

---

CHAPTER II – OBJECTS OF THE SOCIETY

2.1 The main objects of the Society shall be:
(a) To acquire, hold, manage, and maintain the land, building, and common amenities of Shanti Vihar for the benefit of its members.
(b) To provide for the housing, sanitation, water supply, electricity, and other essential services to the members.
(c) To carry on the business of a cooperative housing society, including the collection of maintenance charges, sinking fund contributions, and other levies as decided by the General Body.
(d) To arrange for the repayment of any loans taken for the construction, repair, or improvement of the property.
(e) To undertake such other activities as may be incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects.

---

CHAPTER III – MEMBERSHIP

The registration certificate lists the registered_name of Shanti Vihar Cooperative Housing Society as Shanti Vihar Cooperative Housing Society Limited. Record status: current.

3.1 Eligibility:
Any person competent to contract, who is the owner of a flat in the building of the Society, shall be eligible for membership. The transfer of a flat shall be accompanied by an application for membership in the prescribed form, together with the share certificate and entrance fee as decided by the Managing Committee.

3.2 Admission:
Admission to membership shall be made by the Managing Committee at its meeting, subject to the approval of the General Body in the case of a transfer. The Managing Committee shall communicate its decision within 30 days of receipt of the application. In the event of refusal, the reasons shall be recorded in writing and communicated to the applicant.

3.3 Cessation of Membership:
Membership shall cease upon the transfer of the flat, upon the death of a member (subject to the nomination provisions), or upon expulsion by the General Body for violation of the Bylaws or the Act, provided that the member has been given an opportunity of being heard.

---

CHAPTER IV – SHARE CAPITAL AND FUNDS

4.1 The authorized share capital of the Society shall be Rs. 5,00,000 divided into 5,000 shares of Rs. 100 each. The issued share capital shall be as per the register of members maintained by the Secretary.

4.2 Every member shall hold at least one share of the Society. The share certificate shall be issued under the seal of the Society and the signatures of the Chairman and the Secretary.

4.3 The funds of the Society shall be maintained in a bank account in the name of the Society, operated jointly by the Chairman, the Secretary, and the Treasurer, or any two of them, as decided by the Managing Committee.

---

CHAPTER V – GENERAL BODY

5.1 The General Body shall consist of all the members of the Society. The Annual General Body Meeting shall be held within six months of the close of the financial year.
6.4 Powers of the Managing Committee: Subject to the provisions of the Act, the Rules, and these Bylaws, the Managing Committee shall have the following powers:
a) To admit new members and to maintain the register of members.
b) To maintain the accounts of the Society and to present them to the General Body.
c) To collect from members their share of taxes, assessments, and other outgoings.
d) To arrange for the maintenance and repair of the common areas and the buildings of the Society.
e) To take steps for the recovery of any sums due to the Society.
f) To appoint, suspend, or remove employees of the Society and to fix their remuneration.
g) To institute or defend legal proceedings on behalf of the Society.
h) To do all such acts and things as may be necessary for the proper management of the Society, not inconsistent with the Act, the Rules, and these Bylaws.

6.5 Vacancies: Any vacancy in the Managing Committee caused by death, resignation, or otherwise shall be filled by the Committee by co-option, subject to the approval of the General Body at its next meeting. The member so co-opted shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the Committee.

---

CHAPTER VII – PROPERTY AND BUILDINGS

7.1 The Society is the owner of the land and the buildings standing thereon, including Building No. 1, Building No. 2, Building No. 3, and Building No. 4, together with all common areas, roads, passages, staircases, terraces, compound walls, and open spaces appurtenant thereto. The Society holds the property freehold, as described in the registered conveyance deed dated 14 March 1988, and in the subsequent supplementary deeds.

7.2 The Society shall maintain the buildings and common areas in good repair. The Managing Committee shall be responsible for the upkeep of the external walls, roofs, staircases, lobbies, underground and overhead water tanks, pumps, lifts, electrical installations, and drainage systems.

7.3 Each member shall maintain the interior of his or her flat, including internal plaster, flooring, internal plumbing, and internal electrical wiring. No member shall make any structural alteration to his or her flat, including the removal or addition of any wall, beam, or column, without the prior written permission of the Managing Committee.

7.4 The common areas shall be used by all members for the purpose of access, recreation, and other common amenities. No member shall appropriate any part of the common areas for his or her exclusive use, nor shall any member cause any obstruction or nuisance therein.

7.5 Construction and Age of Buildings: The buildings of the Society were constructed in phases. Building No. 1 and Building No. 2 were completed in 1990. Building No. 4 was completed in 1992. Building No. 3, which is the last of the four buildings to be constructed, was completed in May 1999 and was occupied in the same year. According to the society records, the building_age of Building No. 3 is 25 years. Record status: current. This record is current and is maintained in the property register kept by the Secretary.

7.6 The Society has obtained an occupation certificate and a completion certificate from the local municipal authority for each of the buildings. Copies of these certificates are kept in the office of the Society along with the approved building plans.

7.7 No member shall use his or her flat or any part of the common areas for any purpose other than residential, unless expressly permitted by the General Body.

---

CHAPTER VIII – MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS

8.1 The Managing Committee shall levy a monthly maintenance charge on each member, based on the budget approved by the General Body. The maintenance charge shall be payable in advance by the 10th day of each month.

8.2 The maintenance charge shall cover the cost of:
a) Salaries of the watchman, the cleaner, and the gardener.
b) Electricity charges for common areas, lifts, and water pumps.
c) Water charges and sewerage charges.
d) Repairs to common areas and buildings.
e) Insurance premium for the buildings.
f) Audit fees.
g) Sinking fund contribution, as decided by the General Body.

8.3 The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of repairs, in which the date, nature, and cost of each repair shall be recorded.
CHAPTER IX – PARKING, VEHICLES AND COMMON AREA USE

9.1 The Managing Committee shall frame and revise, from time to time, rules for the allotment and use of parking spaces within the Society premises. Such rules shall be framed keeping in view the total number of parking spaces available, the number of vehicles owned by members, and the convenience and safety of all members and residents.

9.2 The Parking Allocation Policy, as amended by the General Body from time to time, shall be the governing document for all matters relating to parking. The policy document indicates that the policy_revision_date of Parking Allocation Policy is 2023-10-01. Record status: current. The said date is the date on which the current version of the policy was adopted by the General Body at its special meeting held on that day, and the said version is the current and operative version of the policy. Copies of the policy, along with all prior versions, are maintained in the office of the Society and are available for inspection by members.

9.3 No member shall park any vehicle in a space not allotted to him or her, nor shall any member use a parking space for the storage of any goods, materials, or any article other than the vehicle for which the space is allotted.

9.4 Visitors’ parking shall be limited to the spaces earmarked for that purpose. The watchman shall note the registration number of each visitor’s vehicle and the time of entry and exit in a register kept for the purpose. Visitors’ vehicles shall not be parked overnight except with the prior written permission of the Secretary or the Chairperson.

9.5 Two-wheelers shall be parked only in the designated two-wheeler area. No two-wheeler shall be parked in the four-wheeler bays, in the passages, or in front of the entrance to any building. Bicycles and cycles shall be kept in the cycle stand provided near the compound wall.

9.6 The charging of electric vehicles shall be done only at the charging points provided for the purpose and in accordance with the instructions displayed there. No extension cords shall be drawn from any flat or from the common areas for the purpose of charging any vehicle.

9.7 The Managing Committee may, by notice, temporarily close any parking space or part of the parking area for the purpose of repairs, cleaning, or any other work necessary for the maintenance of the Society. During such closure, the members affected shall be accommodated in such alternative spaces as may be available.

9.8 Any vehicle found parked in contravention of the provisions of this Chapter or of the Parking Allocation Policy shall be liable to be towed away or clamped at the owner’s risk and cost. The Managing Committee may also levy a penalty as decided by the General Body, which shall be added to the maintenance bill of the member concerned.

9.9 The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of parking spaces, showing the allotment of each space, the name of the member to whom it is allotted, and the registration number of the vehicle for which it is used. The register shall be updated whenever there is any change in the allotment.

CHAPTER X – WATER, ELECTRICITY AND OTHER UTILITIES

10.1 The Society shall provide water to the members from the common water supply, which shall include the municipal supply, the bore well, and the overhead tanks. The Managing Committee shall ensure that the water supply is maintained and that the tanks are cleaned at regular intervals.

10.2 No member shall waste water or use it for any purpose other than domestic use. No member shall install any pump or other device for drawing water directly from the common supply line without the prior written permission of the Managing Committee.

10.3 The Society shall maintain the electrical installations in the common areas, including the lifts, the water pumps, the corridor lights, and the compound lighting. The electricity charges for the common areas shall be borne by the Society out of the maintenance fund.

10.4 In the event of any breakdown in the water supply or the electrical supply, the Managing Committee shall take immediate steps to restore the same. The Secretary shall record the nature of the breakdown and the date and time of restoration in the register of repairs.

CHAPTER XI – MEMBERS’ RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS

11.1 Every member shall have the right to inspect the books of account, the minutes book, the register of members, and other records of the Society at the registered office during the office hours on any working day, after giving twenty-four hours’ written notice to the Secretary. The inspection shall be carried out in the presence of the Secretary or any person authorised by him in this behalf.

11.2 A member may obtain a copy of any resolution passed by the General Body or the Managing Committee, or of any register or record maintained by the Society, upon payment of such fee as may be fixed by the Managing Committee from time to time. The Secretary shall supply such copy within seven working days of the receipt of the request.

11.3 No member shall use the common areas, including the compound, the staircases, the lobbies, or the terrace, for the storage of personal belongings, for drying of clothes except in the areas designated for the purpose, or for any activity that causes nuisance or obstruction to other members.

11.4 Every member shall intimate to the Secretary, in writing, any change in his address, telephone number, or any other contact details within fifteen days of such change. The Society shall not be responsible for any loss or inconvenience caused to a member due to his failure to intimate such change.

11.5 A member who wishes to transfer his flat, or any share or interest therein, shall comply with the provisions of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Rules, 1961, and the Bye-laws of the Society. The transfer shall be effected only after the transferee has been admitted as a member of the Society.

11.6 The Society shall have a lien on the shares and on the interest in the capital and other funds of the Society, of any member, for any sum due from him to the Society. Such lien may be enforced by the Managing Committee in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the Rules.

---

CHAPTER XII – DISPUTE RESOLUTION

12.1 If any dispute touching the constitution, management, or business of the Society arises between the Society and any member, or between any two or more members, the same shall be referred to the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies having jurisdiction, in accordance with Section 91 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960.

12.2 Before referring any dispute to the Deputy Registrar, the parties to the dispute shall make a bona fide attempt to resolve the matter through the internal dispute resolution mechanism of the Society, as described herein below:

(a) The aggrieved member shall submit a written complaint to the Secretary, setting out the full particulars of the dispute, along with copies of any supporting documents.

(b) The Managing Committee shall consider the complaint at its next meeting, or at a special meeting convened for the purpose within fifteen days of the receipt of the complaint, and shall endeavour to arrive at an amicable settlement.

(c) If the dispute is not resolved at the level of the Managing Committee, it may be referred, at the request of either party, to a committee of three mediators, comprising two members of the Society nominated by the General Body and one independent person, who may be a member of another co-operative housing society in the neighbourhood, nominated by the Managing Committee with the consent of both parties. The mediators shall submit their recommendations in writing within thirty days of their appointment.

(d) The recommendations of the mediators shall be placed before the Managing Committee, which may accept or reject the same. The decision of the Managing Committee shall be communicated to the parties in writing.
CHAPTER XIII – FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

13.1 The financial year of the Society shall commence on the 1st day of April and end on the 31st day of March of the following year.

13.2 The Managing Committee shall cause to be maintained proper books of account and other relevant books and registers as required under the Act, the Rules, and the Bye-laws, with respect to:

(a) all sums of money received and expended by the Society and the matters in respect of which such receipts and expenditure take place;

(b) all sales and purchases of goods and services by the Society;

(c) the assets and liabilities of the Society; and

(d) all other transactions of the Society.

13.3 The books of account shall be kept at the registered office of the Society and shall be open to inspection by any member at all reasonable times, subject to the payment of such fee as may be prescribed by the Managing Committee from time to time, not exceeding rupees ten per inspection. A member desiring such inspection shall give notice in writing to the Secretary at least twenty-four hours in advance.

13.4 All moneys belonging to the Society shall be deposited in the name of the Society in a scheduled bank or in a co-operative bank or in a post office savings account, as may be decided by the Managing Committee. No moneys shall be withdrawn from the bank except by cheques signed by the Treasurer and the Secretary jointly, or by any two office bearers of the Society as may be authorised by the Managing Committee in this behalf.

13.5 The Managing Committee shall, within one month of the close of the financial year, cause a statement of accounts, together with a balance sheet, to be prepared, showing the income and expenditure of the Society during the preceding financial year and the assets and liabilities of the Society as at the close of that year.

13.6 The accounts of the Society shall be audited annually by an auditor appointed by the General Body in its Annual General Meeting. No member of the Managing Committee, and no person who is in the employment of the Society, shall be eligible for appointment as auditor.

13.7 The auditor shall be paid such remuneration as may be fixed by the General Body. The auditor shall have access at all times to the books, accounts, and vouchers of the Society, and shall be entitled to require from the office bearers such information and explanations as may be necessary for the performance of his duties.

13.8 The auditor shall, within such time as may be prescribed, submit his report to the Managing Committee, and the Managing Committee shall cause a copy of such report to be placed before the General Body at its next meeting. A copy of the audit report shall also be forwarded to the Deputy Registrar in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

13.9 MAINTENANCE FUND

(a) The Society shall maintain a separate fund, to be known as the "Maintenance Fund", for the purpose of meeting the day-to-day expenses of the Society, including but not limited to salaries of staff, electricity charges for common areas, water charges, repairs and maintenance of common premises, and such other recurring expenses as may be decided by the Managing Committee.

(b) Every member shall contribute to the Maintenance Fund such amount as may be fixed by the Managing Committee from time to time, subject to the approval of the General Body. The contribution shall be payable monthly in advance, by the 10th day of each calendar month.

(c) If any member fails to pay the contribution to the Maintenance Fund for a period of three consecutive months, the Managing Committee may, after giving fifteen days' notice in writing to such member, charge interest at the rate of fifteen percent per annum on the amount in arrears. The provisions of Chapter XI relating to the lien of the Society on the shares and interest of a member shall apply mutatis mutandis to arrears of maintenance contributions.

13.10 SINKING FUND

(a) The Society shall maintain a separate fund, to be known as the "Sinking Fund", for the purpose of meeting major repairs, replacements, and renovations of the buildings and common amenities of the Society, including but not limited to re-roofing, re-painting, replacement of lifts and water pumps, and such other capital works as may be decided by the General Body.
13.11 SINKING FUND (continued)

(b) The contribution to the Sinking Fund shall be determined by the General Body on the recommendation of the Managing Committee, taking into account the age of the buildings, the anticipated cost of major repairs, and the estimated useful life of the assets concerned. The contribution shall be collected along with the monthly maintenance contribution and shall be credited to the Sinking Fund account maintained separately from the Maintenance Fund.

(c) The Sinking Fund moneys shall be kept in a separate bank account and shall be utilised only for the purposes for which the fund is created. No withdrawal from the Sinking Fund shall be made except by a resolution of the Managing Committee, sanctioned by the General Body, and for a specific purpose approved by the General Body.

(d) The Managing Committee shall, at the end of each financial year, cause a statement of the Sinking Fund to be prepared, showing the total amount collected, the amount expended, the balance in hand, and the interest accrued, and shall place the same before the General Body at its annual general meeting.

13.12 REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE OF BUILDINGS

(a) The Managing Committee shall be responsible for the upkeep and maintenance of the common areas, including but not limited to the external walls, roof, staircases, corridors, lifts, water tanks, drainage lines, compound walls, and the surrounding open spaces.

(b) Repairs of a minor nature, the cost of which does not exceed five thousand rupees in any single instance, may be undertaken by the Secretary or the Treasurer, as the case may be, without prior approval of the Managing Committee, provided that a record of such repairs is maintained and placed before the Managing Committee at its next meeting.

(c) Repairs exceeding five thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees shall require the approval of the Managing Committee. Repairs exceeding fifty thousand rupees shall require the approval of the General Body, except in cases of emergency as provided in clause (d) below.

(d) In case of an emergency, such as a burst pipeline, a major leak, a failure of the lift, or any other situation posing an immediate risk to life or property, the Managing Committee may authorise repairs without prior approval of the General Body, provided that the matter is placed before the General Body at its next meeting for ratification. The Managing Committee shall, in such cases, obtain at least two quotations wherever practicable and shall maintain a record of the steps taken.

13.13 WATER TANKS AND WATER SUPPLY

(a) The Society shall arrange for the cleaning of the overhead and underground water tanks at least twice in every calendar year, and more frequently if required by the health authorities or if the quality of water so demands.

(b) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of tank cleaning, showing the date of cleaning, the name of the agency or person carrying out the cleaning, and the remarks, if any.

(c) No member shall, without the permission of the Managing Committee, carry out any work on the water supply lines or plumbing of the common areas, or interfere with the water supply to other members.

(d) The Society shall take reasonable steps to ensure that the water supplied to the members is potable and that the water storage facilities are maintained in a hygienic condition.

13.14 LIFTS AND OTHER ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS

(a) The Society shall enter into an annual maintenance contract with a reputable agency for the upkeep of the lifts, and the contract shall provide for periodic inspection, servicing, and prompt attendance to breakdowns.

(b) The Managing Committee shall ensure that the lifts are inspected by the competent authority as required under the rules and regulations for the time being in force, and that the necessary certificates are obtained and kept in the Society's records.

(c) The Society shall maintain the electrical installations in the common areas, including the distribution panels, common lighting, and the standby generator, in good working condition. The cost of electricity consumed in the common areas shall be borne by the Society out of the Maintenance Fund.

The AGM minutes state that the resolution_passed of Annual General Meeting 2023 is 2023-08-12. Record status: historical.

The proposed budget for the year 2023-24 was presented. The budget estimated total income of ₹ 52,00,000 and expenditure of ₹ 48,00,000, leaving a projected surplus of ₹ 4,00,000. **Item 5: Discussion on the Rainwater Harvesting Project**

The Chairperson reported that the society had received a directive from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to implement rainwater harvesting measures. The proposal from the sub-committee, which had been studying the matter for the past six months, was presented to the house.

The proposal involved the installation of a recharge pit near the garden area, with a capacity of 20,000 litres, along with the connection of rooftop rainwater pipes to the recharge system. The estimated cost was ₹ 1,80,000. Members discussed the design, and some concerns were raised about the maintenance of the pit. The Secretary noted that the Water & Sanitation sub-committee would include the pit cleaning in its regular schedule.

Mr. Anand Rao, who had been tasked with inspecting the area, reported that a structural engineer had been consulted informally, and the preliminary opinion was that the seepage was due to a failure in the waterproofing membrane of the adjacent retaining wall.

**Item 4: Policy on transfer of shares – revision**

The committee took up the discussion on the policy for transfer of shares, which had been flagged by the Managing Committee at the AGM held earlier this year. The current policy, as per the bye-laws and the standard practice, required a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the society for any transfer. However, there was no clear provision for the transfer of shares to a legal heir in case of death of a member.

The Secretary presented a draft amendment, which proposed that in case of death of a member, the transfer of shares to the legal heir would be processed upon submission of the death certificate, succession certificate or legal heirship certificate, and an indemnity bond, without requiring a separate NOC from the society. The amendment also proposed a simplified procedure for transfer between spouses.

Mr. Kulkarni suggested that the draft be circulated to all members for their comments before it was placed for approval at the next General Body Meeting. The committee agreed that a notice would be put up on the society notice board and circulated on the WhatsApp group, with a 15-day period for comments.

BYLAWS OF THE SOCIETY
(As amended up to the Special General Body Meeting held on 12 January 2024)

---

CHAPTER I – NAME, ADDRESS AND AREA OF OPERATION

1.1 Name of the Society:
The name of the Society shall be "Shanti Vihar Cooperative Housing Society Limited", hereinafter referred to as "the Society". The word "Limited" shall form part of the name of the Society in accordance with section 9(1) of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960.

1.2 Registered Address:
The registered office of the Society shall be at Flat No. A-102, Shanti Vihar, Plot No. 21, Sector 17, Vashi, Navi Mumbai – 400703, or at such other place within the local limits of the Thane District as may be decided by the General Body and approved by the Registrar.

1.3 Area of Operation:
The area of operation of the Society shall be confined to the property known as Shanti Vihar, situate at Plot No. 21, Sector 17, Vashi, Navi Mumbai, together with all structures, common areas, and appurtenances belonging to the Society.

1.4 Liability of Members:
The liability of the members of the Society shall be limited to the amount of share capital subscribed by each member, as provided under section 64 of the Act.

---

CHAPTER II – OBJECTS OF THE SOCIETY

2.1 The main objects of the Society shall be:
(a) To acquire, hold, manage, and maintain the land, building, and common amenities of Shanti Vihar for the benefit of its members.
(b) To provide for the housing, sanitation, water supply, electricity, and other essential services to the members.
(c) To carry on the business of a cooperative housing society, including the collection of maintenance charges, sinking fund contributions, and other levies as decided by the General Body.
(d) To arrange for the repayment of any loans taken for the construction, repair, or improvement of the property.
(e) To undertake such other activities as may be incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects.

---

CHAPTER III – MEMBERSHIP

The registration certificate lists the registered_name of Shanti Vihar Cooperative Housing Society as Shanti Vihar Cooperative Housing Society Limited. Record status: current.

3.1 Eligibility:
Any person competent to contract, who is the owner of a flat in the building of the Society, shall be eligible for membership. The transfer of a flat shall be accompanied by an application for membership in the prescribed form, together with the share certificate and entrance fee as decided by the Managing Committee.

3.2 Admission:
Admission to membership shall be made by the Managing Committee at its meeting, subject to the approval of the General Body in the case of a transfer. The Managing Committee shall communicate its decision within 30 days of receipt of the application. In the event of refusal, the reasons shall be recorded in writing and communicated to the applicant.

3.3 Cessation of Membership:
Membership shall cease upon the transfer of the flat, upon the death of a member (subject to the nomination provisions), or upon expulsion by the General Body for violation of the Bylaws or the Act, provided that the member has been given an opportunity of being heard.

---

CHAPTER IV – SHARE CAPITAL AND FUNDS

4.1 The authorized share capital of the Society shall be Rs. 5,00,000 divided into 5,000 shares of Rs. 100 each. The issued share capital shall be as per the register of members maintained by the Secretary.

4.2 Every member shall hold at least one share of the Society. The share certificate shall be issued under the seal of the Society and the signatures of the Chairman and the Secretary.

4.3 The funds of the Society shall be maintained in a bank account in the name of the Society, operated jointly by the Chairman, the Secretary, and the Treasurer, or any two of them, as decided by the Managing Committee.

---

CHAPTER V – GENERAL BODY

5.1 The General Body shall consist of all the members of the Society. The Annual General Body Meeting shall be held within six months of the close of the financial year.

6.4 Powers of the Managing Committee: Subject to the provisions of the Act, the Rules, and these Bylaws, the Managing Committee shall have the following powers:
a) To admit new members and to maintain the register of members.
b) To maintain the accounts of the Society and to present them to the General Body.
c) To collect from members their share of taxes, assessments, and other outgoings.
d) To arrange for the maintenance and repair of the common areas and the buildings of the Society.
e) To take steps for the recovery of any sums due to the Society.
f) To appoint, suspend, or remove employees of the Society and to fix their remuneration.
g) To institute or defend legal proceedings on behalf of the Society.
h) To do all such acts and things as may be necessary for the proper management of the Society, not inconsistent with the Act, the Rules, and these Bylaws.

6.5 Vacancies: Any vacancy in the Managing Committee caused by death, resignation, or otherwise shall be filled by the Committee by co-option, subject to the approval of the General Body at its next meeting. The member so co-opted shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the Committee.

---

CHAPTER VII – PROPERTY AND BUILDINGS

7.1 The Society is the owner of the land and the buildings standing thereon, including Building No. 1, Building No. 2, Building No. 3, and Building No. 4, together with all common areas, roads, passages, staircases, terraces, compound walls, and open spaces appurtenant thereto. The Society holds the property freehold, as described in the registered conveyance deed dated 14 March 1988, and in the subsequent supplementary deeds.

7.2 The Society shall maintain the buildings and common areas in good repair. The Managing Committee shall be responsible for the upkeep of the external walls, roofs, staircases, lobbies, underground and overhead water tanks, pumps, lifts, electrical installations, and drainage systems.

7.3 Each member shall maintain the interior of his or her flat, including internal plaster, flooring, internal plumbing, and internal electrical wiring. No member shall make any structural alteration to his or her flat, including the removal or addition of any wall, beam, or column, without the prior written permission of the Managing Committee.

7.4 The common areas shall be used by all members for the purpose of access, recreation, and other common amenities. No member shall appropriate any part of the common areas for his or her exclusive use, nor shall any member cause any obstruction or nuisance therein.

7.5 Construction and Age of Buildings: The buildings of the Society were constructed in phases. Building No. 1 and Building No. 2 were completed in 1990. Building No. 4 was completed in 1992. Building No. 3, which is the last of the four buildings to be constructed, was completed in May 1999 and was occupied in the same year. According to the society records, the building_age of Building No. 3 is 25 years. Record status: current. This record is current and is maintained in the property register kept by the Secretary.

7.6 The Society has obtained an occupation certificate and a completion certificate from the local municipal authority for each of the buildings. Copies of these certificates are kept in the office of the Society along with the approved building plans.

7.7 No member shall use his or her flat or any part of the common areas for any purpose other than residential, unless expressly permitted by the General Body.

---

CHAPTER VIII – MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS

8.1 The Managing Committee shall levy a monthly maintenance charge on each member, based on the budget approved by the General Body. The maintenance charge shall be payable in advance by the 10th day of each month.

8.2 The maintenance charge shall cover the cost of:
a) Salaries of the watchman, the cleaner, and the gardener.
b) Electricity charges for common areas, lifts, and water pumps.
c) Water charges and sewerage charges.
d) Repairs to common areas and buildings.
e) Insurance premium for the buildings.
f) Audit fees.
g) Sinking fund contribution, as decided by the General Body.

8.3 The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of repairs, in which the date, nature, and cost of each repair shall be recorded.

CHAPTER IX – PARKING, VEHICLES AND COMMON AREA USE

9.1 The Managing Committee shall frame and revise, from time to time, rules for the allotment and use of parking spaces within the Society premises. Such rules shall be framed keeping in view the total number of parking spaces available, the number of vehicles owned by members, and the convenience and safety of all members and residents.

9.2 The Parking Allocation Policy, as amended by the General Body from time to time, shall be the governing document for all matters relating to parking. The policy document indicates that the policy_revision_date of Parking Allocation Policy is 2023-10-01. Record status: current. The said date is the date on which the current version of the policy was adopted by the General Body at its special meeting held on that day, and the said version is the current and operative version of the policy. Copies of the policy, along with all prior versions, are maintained in the office of the Society and are available for inspection by members.

9.3 No member shall park any vehicle in a space not allotted to him or her, nor shall any member use a parking space for the storage of any goods, materials, or any article other than the vehicle for which the space is allotted.

9.4 Visitors’ parking shall be limited to the spaces earmarked for that purpose. The watchman shall note the registration number of each visitor’s vehicle and the time of entry and exit in a register kept for the purpose. Visitors’ vehicles shall not be parked overnight except with the prior written permission of the Secretary or the Chairperson.

9.5 Two-wheelers shall be parked only in the designated two-wheeler area. No two-wheeler shall be parked in the four-wheeler bays, in the passages, or in front of the entrance to any building. Bicycles and cycles shall be kept in the cycle stand provided near the compound wall.

9.6 The charging of electric vehicles shall be done only at the charging points provided for the purpose and in accordance with the instructions displayed there. No extension cords shall be drawn from any flat or from the common areas for the purpose of charging any vehicle.

9.7 The Managing Committee may, by notice, temporarily close any parking space or part of the parking area for the purpose of repairs, cleaning, or any other work necessary for the maintenance of the Society. During such closure, the members affected shall be accommodated in such alternative spaces as may be available.

9.8 Any vehicle found parked in contravention of the provisions of this Chapter or of the Parking Allocation Policy shall be liable to be towed away or clamped at the owner’s risk and cost. The Managing Committee may also levy a penalty as decided by the General Body, which shall be added to the maintenance bill of the member concerned.

9.9 The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of parking spaces, showing the allotment of each space, the name of the member to whom it is allotted, and the registration number of the vehicle for which it is used. The register shall be updated whenever there is any change in the allotment.

CHAPTER X – WATER, ELECTRICITY AND OTHER UTILITIES

10.1 The Society shall provide water to the members from the common water supply, which shall include the municipal supply, the bore well, and the overhead tanks. The Managing Committee shall ensure that the water supply is maintained and that the tanks are cleaned at regular intervals.

10.2 No member shall waste water or use it for any purpose other than domestic use. No member shall install any pump or other device for drawing water directly from the common supply line without the prior written permission of the Managing Committee.

10.3 The Society shall maintain the electrical installations in the common areas, including the lifts, the water pumps, the corridor lights, and the compound lighting. The electricity charges for the common areas shall be borne by the Society out of the maintenance fund.

10.4 In the event of any breakdown in the water supply or the electrical supply, the Managing Committee shall take immediate steps to restore the same. The Secretary shall record the nature of the breakdown and the date and time of restoration in the register of repairs.

11.4 Every member shall intimate to the Secretary, in writing, any change in his address, telephone number, or any other contact details within fifteen days of such change. The Society shall not be responsible for any loss or inconvenience caused to a member due to his failure to intimate such change.

11.5 A member who wishes to transfer his flat, or any share or interest therein, shall comply with the provisions of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Rules, 1961, and the Bye-laws of the Society. The transfer shall be effected only after the transferee has been admitted as a member of the Society.

11.6 The Society shall have a lien on the shares and on the interest in the capital and other funds of the Society, of any member, for any sum due from him to the Society. Such lien may be enforced by the Managing Committee in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the Rules.

---

CHAPTER XII – DISPUTE RESOLUTION

12.1 If any dispute touching the constitution, management, or business of the Society arises between the Society and any member, or between any two or more members, the same shall be referred to the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies having jurisdiction, in accordance with Section 91 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960.

12.2 Before referring any dispute to the Deputy Registrar, the parties to the dispute shall make a bona fide attempt to resolve the matter through the internal dispute resolution mechanism of the Society, as described herein below:

(a) The aggrieved member shall submit a written complaint to the Secretary, setting out the full particulars of the dispute, along with copies of any supporting documents.

(b) The Managing Committee shall consider the complaint at its next meeting, or at a special meeting convened for the purpose within fifteen days of the receipt of the complaint, and shall endeavour to arrive at an amicable settlement.

(c) If the dispute is not resolved at the level of the Managing Committee, it may be referred, at the request of either party, to a committee of three mediators, comprising two members of the Society nominated by the General Body and one independent person, who may be a member of another co-operative housing society in the neighbourhood, nominated by the Managing Committee with the consent of both parties. The mediators shall submit their recommendations in writing within thirty days of their appointment.

(d) The recommendations of the mediators shall be placed before the Managing Committee, which may accept or reject the same. The decision of the Managing Committee shall be communicated to the parties in writing.

CHAPTER XIII – FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

13.1 The financial year of the Society shall commence on the 1st day of April and end on the 31st day of March of the following year.

13.2 The Managing Committee shall cause to be maintained proper books of account and other relevant books and registers as required under the Act, the Rules, and the Bye-laws, with respect to:

(a) all sums of money received and expended by the Society and the matters in respect of which such receipts and expenditure take place;

(b) all sales and purchases of goods and services by the Society;

(c) the assets and liabilities of the Society; and

(d) all other transactions of the Society.

13.3 The books of account shall be kept at the registered office of the Society and shall be open to inspection by any member at all reasonable times, subject to the payment of such fee as may be prescribed by the Managing Committee from time to time, not exceeding rupees ten per inspection. A member desiring such inspection shall give notice in writing to the Secretary at least twenty-four hours in advance.

13.4 All moneys belonging to the Society shall be deposited in the name of the Society in a scheduled bank or in a co-operative bank or in a post office savings account, as may be decided by the Managing Committee. No moneys shall be withdrawn from the bank except by cheques signed by the Treasurer and the Secretary jointly, or by any two office bearers of the Society as may be authorised by the Managing Committee in this behalf.

13.5 The Managing Committee shall, within one month of the close of the financial year, cause a statement of accounts, together with a balance sheet, to be prepared, showing the income and expenditure of the Society during the preceding financial year and the assets and liabilities of the Society as at the close of that year.

13.6 The accounts of the Society shall be audited annually by an auditor appointed by the General Body in its Annual General Meeting. No member of the Managing Committee, and no person who is in the employment of the Society, shall be eligible for appointment as auditor.

13.7 The auditor shall be paid such remuneration as may be fixed by the General Body. The auditor shall have access at all times to the books, accounts, and vouchers of the Society, and shall be entitled to require from the office bearers such information and explanations as may be necessary for the performance of his duties.

13.8 The auditor shall, within such time as may be prescribed, submit his report to the Managing Committee, and the Managing Committee shall cause a copy of such report to be placed before the General Body at its next meeting. A copy of the audit report shall also be forwarded to the Deputy Registrar in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

13.9 MAINTENANCE FUND

(a) The Society shall maintain a separate fund, to be known as the "Maintenance Fund", for the purpose of meeting the day-to-day expenses of the Society, including but not limited to salaries of staff, electricity charges for common areas, water charges, repairs and maintenance of common premises, and such other recurring expenses as may be decided by the Managing Committee.

(b) Every member shall contribute to the Maintenance Fund such amount as may be fixed by the Managing Committee from time to time, subject to the approval of the General Body. The contribution shall be payable monthly in advance, by the 10th day of each calendar month.

(c) If any member fails to pay the contribution to the Maintenance Fund for a period of three consecutive months, the Managing Committee may, after giving fifteen days' notice in writing to such member, charge interest at the rate of fifteen percent per annum on the amount in arrears. The provisions of Chapter XI relating to the lien of the Society on the shares and interest of a member shall apply mutatis mutandis to arrears of maintenance contributions.

13.10 SINKING FUND

(a) The Society shall maintain a separate fund, to be known as the "Sinking Fund", for the purpose of meeting major repairs, replacements, and renovations of the buildings and common amenities of the Society, including but not limited to re-roofing, re-painting, replacement of lifts and water pumps, and such other capital works as may be decided by the General Body.

13.11 SINKING FUND (continued)

(b) The contribution to the Sinking Fund shall be determined by the General Body on the recommendation of the Managing Committee, taking into account the age of the buildings, the anticipated cost of major repairs, and the estimated useful life of the assets concerned. The contribution shall be collected along with the monthly maintenance contribution and shall be credited to the Sinking Fund account maintained separately from the Maintenance Fund.

(c) The Sinking Fund moneys shall be kept in a separate bank account and shall be utilised only for the purposes for which the fund is created. No withdrawal from the Sinking Fund shall be made except by a resolution of the Managing Committee, sanctioned by the General Body, and for a specific purpose approved by the General Body.

(d) The Managing Committee shall, at the end of each financial year, cause a statement of the Sinking Fund to be prepared, showing the total amount collected, the amount expended, the balance in hand, and the interest accrued, and shall place the same before the General Body at its annual general meeting.

13.12 REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE OF BUILDINGS

(a) The Managing Committee shall be responsible for the upkeep and maintenance of the common areas, including but not limited to the external walls, roof, staircases, corridors, lifts, water tanks, drainage lines, compound walls, and the surrounding open spaces.

(b) Repairs of a minor nature, the cost of which does not exceed five thousand rupees in any single instance, may be undertaken by the Secretary or the Treasurer, as the case may be, without prior approval of the Managing Committee, provided that a record of such repairs is maintained and placed before the Managing Committee at its next meeting.

(c) Repairs exceeding five thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees shall require the approval of the Managing Committee. Repairs exceeding fifty thousand rupees shall require the approval of the General Body, except in cases of emergency as provided in clause (d) below.

(d) In case of an emergency, such as a burst pipeline, a major leak, a failure of the lift, or any other situation posing an immediate risk to life or property, the Managing Committee may authorise repairs without prior approval of the General Body, provided that the matter is placed before the General Body at its next meeting for ratification. The Managing Committee shall, in such cases, obtain at least two quotations wherever practicable and shall maintain a record of the steps taken.

13.13 WATER TANKS AND WATER SUPPLY

(a) The Society shall arrange for the cleaning of the overhead and underground water tanks at least twice in every calendar year, and more frequently if required by the health authorities or if the quality of water so demands.

(b) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of tank cleaning, showing the date of cleaning, the name of the agency or person carrying out the cleaning, and the remarks, if any.

(c) No member shall, without the permission of the Managing Committee, carry out any work on the water supply lines or plumbing of the common areas, or interfere with the water supply to other members.

(d) The Society shall take reasonable steps to ensure that the water supplied to the members is potable and that the water storage facilities are maintained in a hygienic condition.

13.14 LIFTS AND OTHER ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS

(a) The Society shall enter into an annual maintenance contract with a reputable agency for the upkeep of the lifts, and the contract shall provide for periodic inspection, servicing, and prompt attendance to breakdowns.

(b) The Managing Committee shall ensure that the lifts are inspected by the competent authority as required under the rules and regulations for the time being in force, and that the necessary certificates are obtained and kept in the Society's records.

(c) The Society shall maintain the electrical installations in the common areas, including the distribution panels, common lighting, and the standby generator, in good working condition. The cost of electricity consumed in the common areas shall be borne by the Society out of the Maintenance Fund.

The minutes of the meeting held on 28/05/23 were circulated to all members by email and also kept in the society office for inspection. No suggestions or corrections were received from any member. The minutes were confirmed unanimously.

---

**Item 2: Follow-up on seepage in basement parking**

The Chairperson called for a status update on the seepage issue in the basement parking near the lift lobby. Mr. Anand Rao reported that he had received an informal verbal opinion from a structural engineer, Mr. Fernandes, who had inspected the area at no cost. The engineer's preliminary view was that the seepage was due to a failure in the waterproofing membrane of the adjacent retaining wall. Mr. Rao stressed that this was only an informal opinion and that a formal inspection with a written report would be required before any major work was undertaken.

The committee discussed the history of the problem. Patch repairs had been carried out in November 2021 and again in March 2022, but the seepage had returned within a few months each time. The plaster on the wall near the lift lobby was showing damp patches and some efflorescence. Mrs. Menon suggested that the society should not spend further money on patch repairs and should instead commission a proper investigation.

After discussion, the committee resolved:

- To obtain quotations from two structural engineers for a detailed inspection and written report.
- The report should include the likely cause of the seepage, the recommended method of repair (including whether the waterproofing membrane needed to be replaced), and an estimate of costs.
- The Secretary was asked to invite quotations by 20/06/23.

Action: Mr. Anand Rao and the Secretary to shortlist engineers and present quotations at the next meeting.

---

**Item 3: Rainwater harvesting project – updates**

The Secretary reported on the progress of the rainwater harvesting project approved at the AGM. The work order had been issued to M/s. GreenAqua Solutions on 02/06/23. The contractor had commenced work on 05/06/23. Excavation for the recharge pit near the garden area was in progress.

The contractor had requested a small change in the position of the recharge pit, moving it approximately two feet towards the boundary wall, to avoid an existing underground drain line that was discovered during excavation. The Water & Sanitation sub-committee had reviewed the request and had no objection, provided the pit remained at least four feet away from the compound wall foundation. The committee approved this minor shift.

The contractor has stated that the work will be completed within six weeks from the start date, i.e., by 17/07/23. The committee noted that the BMC directive requires completion by end of July 2023.

Action: The Secretary to monitor progress and report at the next meeting.

---

**Item 4: Repair of eastern compound wall**

The Chairperson informed the committee that the BMC had also issued a notice regarding the condition of the eastern compound wall, which was showing visible bulging in one section near the rear gate. This was an old wall, and a portion had developed cracks. The BMC notice had given the society sixty days to carry out repairs or reconstruction.

The committee discussed the two quotations received for the repair work:

1. M/s. Kamble Constructions – ₹ 4,85,000 for repair and strengthening of the existing wall, including new plaster and a coat of waterproofing.
2. M/s. Patil Builders – ₹ 5,20,000 for demolition and reconstruction of the affected section (about 40 feet) with new foundations.

Shree Construction had quoted ₹ 4,60,000 for repair and strengthening of the existing wall, with a note that the scope included partial demolition of the bulged section (approximately 15 feet) and rebuilding it with new bricks, along with plaster and waterproofing for the entire wall length.

**MINUTES OF THE MANAGING COMMITTEE MEETING – SHANTI VIHAR COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY LTD.**

**Date:** 03/07/2023 (Monday)
**Time:** 7:30 PM
**Venue:** Society Office / Committee Room
**Presided by:** Mr. A. Deshpande (Chairman)
**Attendees:** As per attendance sheet attached. Quorum present.

---

**Item 1: Confirmation of minutes of the previous meeting (MC/26/06/2023)**

The minutes of the meeting held on 26/06/2023 were read out. Two members suggested minor corrections to the wording of Resolution No. MC/26/06/2023/01, regarding the payment to M/s. GreenAqua Solutions. The Secretary confirmed that the resolution text was accurate as recorded. The minutes were confirmed as a correct record of the proceedings.

**Item 2: Rainwater harvesting project – site status and second running bill**

The Chairman gave an update on the rainwater harvesting project. The excavation and filter media installation were complete. The contractor, M/s. GreenAqua Solutions, had commenced commissioning work, including flushing of the filter beds and testing of the recharge well.

The Secretary presented the second running bill from the contractor, amounting to ₹ 1,20,000, covering the cost of the pump, control panel, and piping for the overflow line. The bill was examined. The Treasurer noted that the total expenditure on the project to date, including the first running bill, was ₹ 3,05,000, which was within the approved budget of ₹ 4,50,000.

*Resolution No. MC/03/07/2023/01:* The committee approved the payment of ₹ 1,20,000 to M/s. GreenAqua Solutions towards the second running bill. The Treasurer was authorised to issue the cheque after verification of the GST invoice and delivery challan.

**Item 3: Eastern compound wall – finalisation of quotation**

The committee discussed the three quotations for the repair of the eastern compound wall, in continuation of the previous meeting. The quotations were:

1. M/s. Kamble Constructions – ₹ 4,85,000 (repair and strengthening)
2. M/s. Patil Builders – ₹ 5,20,000 (demolition and reconstruction)
3. M/s. Shree Construction – ₹ 4,60,000 (repair, partial demolition of 15 ft bulged section, rebuilding, plaster and waterproofing)

Mr. Nair noted that the quotation from M/s. Shree Construction was the most economical and also included the necessary partial demolition. After discussion, the committee decided to accept the quotation from M/s. Shree Construction.

*Resolution No. MC/03/07/2023/02:* The committee accepted the quotation of ₹ 4,60,000 from M/s. Shree Construction for the repair of the eastern compound wall. The Chairman and Secretary were authorised to sign the work order and agreement. The work is to be completed within 45 days.

**Item 4: Policy on transfer of shares – revision**

The committee took up the discussion on the policy for transfer of shares, which had been flagged by the Managing Committee at the AGM held earlier this year. The current policy, as per the bye-laws and the standard practice, required a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the society for any transfer. However, there was no clear provision for the transfer of shares to a legal heir in case of death of a member.

The Secretary presented a draft amendment, which proposed that in case of death of a member, the transfer of shares to the legal heir would be processed upon submission of the death certificate, succession certificate or legal heirship certificate, and an indemnity bond, without requiring a separate NOC from the society. The amendment also proposed a simplified procedure for transfer between spouses.

Mr. Kulkarni suggested that the draft be circulated to all members for their comments before it was placed for approval at the next General Body Meeting. The committee agreed that a notice would be put up on the society notice board and circulated on the WhatsApp group, with a 15-day period for comments.

*Resolution No. MC/03/07/2023/03:* The committee approved the draft amendment to the policy on transfer of shares, to be circulated for member comments, and to be placed for approval at the next General Body Meeting.
